body:
# Independent audit of the corrected pure-abnormal section reduction

The corrected complete note
`candidate ce2469e6ba848252` passes an
independent audit. This audit specifically checks the newly inserted
positive-base restriction and saturated-lattice reduction; it does not
reuse an audit of the earlier, uncorrected induction statement.

## 1. The correction removes the actual zero-fiber defect

Let P consist of the positive d-volume integer fibers. If an integer
base belongs to conv(P), Minkowski interpolation of positive-volume
fibers puts a positive-volume body in that fiber. Thus
`conv(P) intersect Z^n=P`, exactly as stated.

Restriction to `conv(P) x R^d` leaves every positive original integer
fiber unchanged, removes all other integer bases, and therefore leaves
the entire original mixed measure unchanged. In particular every cap
mass and hinge is the same function of ALL cap coefficients before
and after restriction, not merely equal at the chosen parameters.
The selected effective derivative traces are also unchanged when,
as the note assumes, they come from consistent physical cap gradients:
an original zero-d-volume fiber contributes the identically zero
function and hence zero derivative source. Its nonzero geometric
(d-1)-section, if any, is not an admissible extra derivative source.

The displayed square-to-segment example demonstrates precisely the
original error: geometric section mass at the removed base one would
otherwise lie outside the bases where the cover is imposed. Its
removal is necessary, and the revised argument actually removes it.

## 2. The affine lattice reduction is valid

The span E of the integer differences of P has dimension m, and
`Gamma=E intersect Z^n` is a saturated rank-m subgroup. The primitive
vector and Euclidean row-operation induction extends its lattice basis
to a unimodular basis: after sending a primitive vector to e_1,
subtracting first coordinates leaves a saturated subgroup of the last
n-1 coordinates. This proves the asserted transformation without an
untracked finite-index sublattice.

Translation by a point of P, application of that unimodular map, and
deletion of identically zero base coordinates produce exactly Z^m as
the remaining base lattice. The convex hull of balls in m+1 affinely
independent positive fibers has full relative dimension m+d, proving
that the restricted/reduced source really is a convex body in the
new ambient space. This includes m=0.

Continuous coordinates are unchanged, so all continuous fiber d-volume
and section (d-1)-volume sums are unchanged. No preservation of
ambient Hausdorff measure under the base map is needed or claimed.
The transformed base moment is exactly the retained part of
`U(Z_i-z_0 S_i)`, and subtracting z_0 times the mass equation before
applying U gives the transformed contact balance. All scalar margins
and the continuous normal span are preserved.

## 3. Coarea and the legitimate conditional induction

A cap of source mass strictly between zero and M has strict-sign source
points on both sides. Since relative interior points are dense in the
reduced full-dimensional convex body, both can be approximated by
interior points without changing their signs; their segment proves
that the cutting plane meets the interior. Its section is consequently
a convex body of relative dimension m+d-1.

The continuous rotation, the lattice-preserving fiber shear, and the
deletion of the plane coordinate identify each integer section with
its actual continuous (d-1)-dimensional Euclidean section. There is
no extra ambient graph Jacobian. For a nonunit continuous normal,
the coarea factor is the single constant 1/|u_i| and cancels from
normalized section depth. Formula (4) for every restricted cap is
correct, including whole, empty, and vertical restrictions.

The other caps cover the entire plane at every retained base: if all
their margins were strictly negative at a plane point, a small motion
in direction -u_i would make the i-th margin negative while preserving
all the others' strict signs, contradicting whole-space coverage.
Finiteness of the cap family supplies one common motion size.

Under the explicitly required full-geometric-trace hypothesis and
S_i>0, the section union has intrinsic dimension exactly d-1. The
induction hypothesis OC(m,d-1) therefore applies to exactly this
source, and its selected point necessarily has a base in P. Coverage
by some cap other than i then proves (5) with
`gamma_(d-1)/2^m`, without exchanging a maximum and a sum. The zero
ambient-dimensional case m=0,d=1 is correctly handled as a single
point instead of invoking OC at an excluded parameter pair.

## 4. The pure stress equations and the rank projection

With zero objective multiplier, the source-cap volume and hinge terms
in the normal equations disappear. Taking the dot product of the
unsimplified i-th normal equation with u_i gives zero sphere
multiplier: the section and assigned contacts satisfy L_i=0, and the
mass and base-moment equations cancel the remaining offset terms.
Projection to V causes no error because u_i belongs to V.

The individual continuous equation is only its V projection. The
common-rotation variation makes the summed section-normal tensor
symmetric; its V projection is zero and all its right factors lie in
V, so the full summed tensor is zero. This does not determine each
individual perpendicular section moment. The note now states this
limitation correctly.

Each cross-margin equation uses only normals in V, so the projected
individual equation is sufficient for (3). Positive r_i S_i gives a
genuine convex combination of assigned contacts, with total weight
r_i S_i. Its base coordinate may be fractional, and neither source
membership nor identity with the point supplied by OC is inferred.

## 5. Both obstruction examples are exact

For the triangular prism facet, the three perturbed planes cut properly
exactly over their small corner triangles. Their physical coarea
measures converge to the three corner indicators, and averaging the
actual limiting gradients gives the stated consistent trace. Its
centroid is zero, each covering barycentric halfplane has exactly one
third of its mass, and every through-zero halfplane contains a full
corner cluster since `(1-3epsilon) max ell(p_i)>0`. Thus its maximum
depth is exactly 1/3, strictly below gamma_2. The trace is not the
uniform geometric section measure; the full-trace qualification is
essential.

In the binary-height example, every fiber is exact because its base is
extreme, and the cutting plane misses all four intervals. The hinge
lower bound follows by retaining the positive linear term at each of
the appropriate two diagonal pairs; affine functions have equal sums
on the two diagonals, and b>=a closes the estimate. The zero thresholds
attain 4L. The budget endpoint is one half by the union bound. All cap
gradients vanish locally, so the displayed nonzero pure abnormal stress
with no section mass is valid. An objective-one stress also exists:
take r_i=0, eta_z=1, and at every base the contact x=0 with the two
normal weights 1/2. Its source moments satisfy the corresponding
normal equations with each hinge 2L.

Both examples are scoped correctly: neither is claimed to be a
below-OC abnormal minimizer. The corrected note proves the stated
conditional section-overlap constraint, not the missing ambient
cap-volume contradiction. No further correction is needed.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
